Read poly(A)/poly(T) tail coordinates for the cDNA pipeline

Source: R/ninetails_core_functions_cDNA_model.R
read_tail_coordinates_cdna.Rd

Converts the tail coordinates produced by Lachesis or Dorado into one common table used by the cDNA pipeline, so that the downstream functions do not depend on the tool that delimited the tail.

Usage

read_tail_coordinates_cdna(tail_coordinates, source = "lachesis")

Arguments

tail_coordinates

Character string or data frame. Path to the Lachesis output / Dorado summary file, or the same table in memory.

source

Character string ["lachesis"]. Tool that produced the coordinates: "lachesis" or "dorado".

Value

A data frame with one row per read:

read_id

Character. Read identifier

filename

Character. POD5 file name (NA if not available)

contig

Character. Reference name (NA if not available)

tail_start

Numeric. First sample of the tail (0-based)

tail_end

Numeric. End of the tail (exclusive)

polya_length

Numeric. Estimated tail length in nucleotides

qc_tag

Character. Lachesis QC tag or Dorado mapping quality

tail_type

Character. "polyA", "polyT", "unidentified" or NA

Details

Coordinates are positions in the raw signal (samples), with the tail spanning signal[(tail_start + 1):tail_end].

Lachesis input

The tail is delimited by adapter_end and polya_end in both orientations. The orientation is taken from the strand column: "+" is a poly(A) read, "-" is a poly(T) read.

Dorado input

The tail is delimited by poly_tail_start and poly_tail_end. The summary does not carry the read orientation, so tail_type is NA and has to be filled in by the caller (see detect_orientation_multiple). Both alignment_mapq and alignment_mapping_quality, as well as filename and input_filename, are accepted.

See also

extract_tail_signals_cdna, check_tails_dorado_cDNA

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{

coordinates <- ninetails::read_tail_coordinates_cdna(
  tail_coordinates = '/path/to/lachesis_polya.tsv',
  source = "lachesis")

} # }
